chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abi Basir, from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds, but He follows them from among them those who follow Satan and are led astray.'
He said: This is the meaning of Allah's saying: 'His authority is only over those who take him as their master and their associates.'
His authority is only over those who take him as their master and their associates.
And he said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted, granted Satan authority over whoever abandoned acting according to His Book and followed his own desires.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Satan's authority over believers and those who follow him?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the Shia doctrine of *al-Sulṭān al-Mubin* (the Clear Authority), emphasizing that Satan's dominion is not absolute but contingent upon human free will (*ikhtiyar*). This distinction reinforces the theological principle that believers are shielded from his influence through divine grace and conscious adherence to righteous deeds, while those who actively choose his path fall under his sway.
